bundles.name: automation
bundles.description: Trigger-based field workflows, usually driving Termux scripts.

bundles.name: comms
bundles.description: Engagement communications, including self-hostable and offline-capable options.

bundles.name: core
bundles.description: Termux itself, its add-on APKs, and the terminal essentials. Installed by every profile.

bundles.name: credaccess
bundles.description: Password managers, TOTP and engagement-scoped credential storage.

bundles.name: desktop
bundles.description: Linux desktop backends for the phone. Pluggable: KeX today, AVF later.

bundles.name: dev
bundles.description: Editors, runtimes and the shell environment.

bundles.name: device
bundles.description: App and device control: Shizuku, debloat, work-profile isolation, and the root stack.

bundles.name: egress
bundles.description: Firewall, VPN, Tor and proxying: control over where the traffic goes.

bundles.name: hardware
bundles.description: NFC, RFID, BLE and USB OTG serial — the bench hardware interface.

bundles.name: labs
bundles.description: Deliberately vulnerable targets to practise against. PAUSED — not in any profile yet.

bundles.name: mobile
bundles.description: Mobile application assessment: decompile, patch, hook, intercept.

bundles.name: network
bundles.description: Capture, scan, map and intercept the network the device is on.

bundles.name: radio
bundles.description: Software defined radio, GNSS and LoRa.

bundles.name: recon
bundles.description: OSINT and pre-engagement reconnaissance, including offline mapping.

bundles.name: reference
bundles.description: Offline methodology, standards and wordlists.

bundles.name: remote
bundles.description: Remote access, file transfer and getting artifacts off the device.

bundles.name: reporting
bundles.description: Evidence capture, notes and the reporting pipeline.

bundles.name: server
bundles.description: Servers and listeners run from the phone. PAUSED — not in any profile yet.

bundles.name: smoke
bundles.description: Four small tools, one per install mechanism, for proving a fresh install works end to end. Deliberately tiny: the point is to exercise every code path in the engine, not to be useful.

bundles.name: socialeng
bundles.description: Social engineering support. Read the legal notes before using any of it.

bundles.name: web
bundles.description: Web and API testing, including the on-device intercepting proxies.

bundles.name: wireless
bundles.description: Wardriving and wireless attack tooling. Most of it needs a NetHunter kernel and an external adapter.

profiles.name: android-smoke
profiles.description: Smoke test. Installs four small tools, one per mechanism — an apt package, a pip package, a Go module and a shallow clone — so one run tells you whether a fresh install actually works. Use this before trusting any bigger profile.

profiles.name: android-minimal
profiles.description: Termux and a working shell, nothing else. The floor everything is built on, and a sane thing to put on a phone you have not decided about yet.

profiles.name: android-stock
profiles.description: Everything that works on a completely untouched device. No bootloader unlock, no root, no warranty voided, and Play Integrity stays intact. Roughly nine tenths of the catalogue.

profiles.name: android-rf
profiles.description: A focused radio and hardware bench: SDR, GNSS, LoRa, NFC, RFID, BLE and the OTG serial console. Runs on a stock device — most of this needs no privileges, only an adapter.

profiles.name: android-shizuku
profiles.description: Stock plus Shizuku, paired over wireless debugging. ADB-level privileges with no root, no PC on Android 11+, and nothing irreversible. If you do exactly one thing past stock, do this.

profiles.name: android-rooted
profiles.description: Magisk or KernelSU. Unlocks raw sockets, privileged ports, Frida, real tcpdump and LSPosed. This is also where Play Integrity stops working — use a dedicated device.

profiles.name: android-nethunter
profiles.description: A supported device running a NetHunter kernel. Monitor mode, packet injection, HID attacks and external adapter drivers. The tier that can brick a phone.

tools.name: Automate
tools.desc: Flowchart-based automation. The third option, and the most visual.

tools.name: Home Assistant
tools.desc: Companion app, and a surprisingly good generic sensor and webhook source for automations.
tools.notes: The F-Droid build is the 'minimal' flavour, which drops the Play Services dependencies.

tools.name: MacroDroid
tools.desc: Friendlier automation with a gentler learning curve. Less powerful than Tasker.

tools.name: Tasker
tools.desc: Combined with Termux:Tasker this is how field workflows get built — trigger a script on arriving at a location, on a WiFi join, on a notification.

tools.name: Briar
tools.desc: Peer-to-peer messaging over Tor, WiFi or Bluetooth, with no server at all. Works when the network does not.

tools.name: Element
tools.desc: Matrix client. Self-hostable, so team comms during an engagement can stay on infrastructure you control.

tools.name: ntfy
tools.desc: Open source push notifications, self-hostable. Where honeypot and canary alerts land.

tools.name: Pushover
tools.desc: Commercial push notifications. Simpler than ntfy if you do not want to host anything.

tools.name: Signal
tools.desc: Default for engagement comms. The GitHub build avoids Play Services where you would rather not have it.

tools.name: Telegram
tools.desc: Client-driven. Keep it if your clients use it.
tools.notes: Not in the main F-Droid repo.

tools.name: ConnectBot
tools.desc: Lightweight open source SSH client. No account, no sync, no telemetry.

tools.name: Hacker's Keyboard
tools.desc: A keyboard with real Ctrl, Alt, Esc, Tab, arrows and function keys. Non-negotiable for terminal work.

tools.name: Kali NetHunter
tools.desc: Kali's Android platform. Rootless mode installs a full Kali chroot on a stock unrooted phone; full mode needs a NetHunter kernel.
tools.notes: Rootless works on any device. Monitor mode and HID attacks need Tier 3.

tools.name: NetHunter Store
tools.desc: Offensive Security's app repository. The supported source for the NetHunter apps.

tools.name: Termius
tools.desc: Polished SSH and SFTP client with cross-device sync. Free tier is usable; sync is paid.

tools.name: Termux
tools.desc: Terminal emulator and full Linux package environment. The backbone of the whole toolkit — everything in here that matters most is a Termux package, not an APK.
tools.notes: F-Droid or GitHub only. The Play Store build is abandoned and its packages are years stale.

tools.name: Termux:API
tools.desc: Bridges the shell to SMS, clipboard, sensors, camera, GPS, notifications and TTS. Every interesting automation script needs it.
tools.notes: Also requires 'pkg install termux-api' inside Termux.

tools.name: Termux:Boot
tools.desc: Run scripts at device boot. Needed for anything that has to survive a reboot — listeners, honeypots, sync jobs.

tools.name: Termux:Float
tools.desc: A floating terminal window over other apps. Useful when you need a shell while driving a GUI tool.

tools.name: Termux:Styling
tools.desc: Fonts and colour schemes for Termux. Where the androidWTF theme gets applied.

tools.name: Termux:Tasker
tools.desc: Exposes Termux scripts as Tasker actions. Combined with Tasker this is the automation backbone.

tools.name: Termux:Widget
tools.desc: Home screen shortcuts that launch a script with one tap. This is how field workflows get usable.

tools.name: Termux:X11
tools.desc: X11 display server for Termux, for running GUI Linux applications.
tools.notes: Pairs with the Linux Desktop module.

tools.name: Aegis Authenticator
tools.desc: Open source TOTP with an encrypted, exportable vault. Prefer it over Google Authenticator — you can actually get your seeds back out.

tools.name: Bitwarden
tools.desc: Password manager. Self-hostable with Vaultwarden if you would rather not use their cloud.
tools.notes: No longer in the main F-Droid repo — GitHub Releases or Play.

tools.name: Google Authenticator
tools.desc: Same reasoning. Keep it for client accounts, not your own.

tools.name: Cracking — do it elsewhere
tools.desc: Not an app. There is no usable GPU acceleration path for hashcat on Android. Capture on the phone, crack on the homelab.
tools.notes: john the ripper runs in Termux on CPU, and is slow enough to be a novelty.

tools.name: KeePassDX
tools.desc: Offline KDBX vault. Useful for engagement-scoped credentials you want kept out of your personal manager entirely.

tools.name: Microsoft Authenticator
tools.desc: Needed for client Entra tenants whether you like it or not.

tools.name: Android Linux Terminal
tools.desc: Not an app. Android 15+ ships a native Linux terminal on the Android Virtualization Framework — a real VM with a real kernel, not PRoot. It will obsolete most of this category.
tools.notes: Enable in Developer Options where your device supports it. Design the Linux layer with a pluggable backend so you can move to this.

tools.name: DroidDesk
tools.desc: Community desktop option. Supported as a documented recipe that shells out to their installer, never as vendored code.
tools.notes: GPL-3.0. Bundling or linking its code would make androidWTF GPL-3.0 too. Their own COMPLIANCE.md flags unresolved provenance issues.

tools.name: NetHunter KeX
tools.desc: Full Kali desktop over VNC. Offensive Security maintained, works in NetHunter Rootless on a stock phone. The recommended desktop backend.
tools.notes: Needs a VNC client — RealVNC Viewer is the reliable one.

tools.name: Termux:X11 + XFCE
tools.desc: A lighter desktop straight out of Termux, no chroot involved. Faster than VNC, fewer batteries included.

tools.name: Acode
tools.desc: Capable code editor with plugin support and SFTP. The better default of the mobile editors.

tools.name: git
tools.desc: Version control, and how most of the catalogue's source actually arrives.

tools.name: GitHub
tools.desc: Issues, PRs and code review from the phone.

tools.name: Go
tools.desc: Needed to build the ProjectDiscovery tooling from source when a package lags.

tools.name: neovim
tools.desc: The editor you already use, in Termux, with your existing config.

tools.name: Node.js
tools.desc: Runs Juice Shop and most of the JS-based tooling directly.

tools.name: Python
tools.desc: The runtime most of the tooling in here is written in.

tools.name: ripgrep / fd / jq
tools.desc: The search and parse trio. You will use these more than anything else in here.

tools.name: Spck Editor
tools.desc: Git-aware editor with a built-in preview. Alternative to Acode.

tools.name: Starship
tools.desc: The prompt, shared with the other WTF builds so every shell looks the same.

tools.name: tmux
tools.desc: Sessions that survive Termux being backgrounded and killed. Not optional on a phone.

tools.name: Aurora Store
tools.desc: Play Store apps without a Google account, using anonymous sessions.
tools.notes: Anonymous sessions break periodically. Paid apps still need a real account.

tools.name: Insular
tools.desc: Work profile isolation, a fork of Island. Alternative to Shelter — pick one.

tools.name: Obtainium
tools.desc: Installs and auto-updates sideloaded apps straight from GitHub Releases, F-Droid and arbitrary URLs. Without this, maintaining seventy sideloaded APKs by hand is what kills the project in six months.
tools.notes: androidWTF ships an Obtainium config you can import in one go.

tools.name: Shelter
tools.desc: Runs the catalogue inside an isolated Android work profile you can freeze when you are not on an engagement. Keeps the pentest apps away from your banking apps.

tools.name: Shizuku
tools.desc: Grants apps ADB-level privileges with no root, by pairing over wireless debugging. On Android 11+ this needs no PC at all. The single highest-value install in the catalogue after Termux.
tools.notes: Installing it is Tier 0; the privileges it unlocks are Tier 1. Must be re-paired after every reboot unless rooted.

tools.name: App Manager
tools.desc: Manifest viewer, component blocker, AppOps control, signature checks, APK extraction and tracker analysis. Best-in-class, and directly useful for mobile app assessments.

tools.name: Canta
tools.desc: Uninstall system bloat through Shizuku, with a crowd-sourced safety rating per package. The debloat engine.

tools.name: KernelSU
tools.desc: Kernel-based root, an alternative to Magisk on supported kernels.

tools.name: LSPosed
tools.desc: Xposed framework for hooking app internals at runtime. The base for SSL unpinning modules.

tools.name: Magisk
tools.desc: Systemless root. The gate for everything in Tier 2.
tools.notes: Breaks Play Integrity. Banking, payment and MDM apps will refuse to run.

tools.name: TrustMeAlready
tools.desc: Xposed module that disables SSL verification and pinning system-wide, so an intercepting proxy can see app traffic.
tools.notes: Needed for most real mobile app assessments. objection can do the same per-process without a module.

tools.name: cloudflared
tools.desc: Expose a service running on the phone to the internet without a public IP.
tools.notes: Also useful for getting a callback to a device behind carrier NAT.

tools.name: Every Proxy
tools.desc: Turns the phone into an HTTP and SOCKS5 proxy. Genuinely handy for pivoting a laptop through the phone's connection.

tools.name: NetGuard
tools.desc: Per-app firewall with no root, via the VPN service. The simpler, more predictable option.
tools.notes: Same VPN slot conflict. Pick one of NetGuard or RethinkDNS.

tools.name: OpenVPN for Android
tools.desc: Open source OpenVPN client. Plenty of clients still hand you a .ovpn file.

tools.name: Orbot
tools.desc: Tor as a transparent proxy or VPN for selected apps.
tools.notes: Not in the main F-Droid repo — Guardian Project run their own, or take it from GitHub Releases.

tools.name: proxychains-ng
tools.desc: Force any Termux CLI tool through a SOCKS proxy.

tools.name: RethinkDNS
tools.desc: Per-app firewall, DNS filtering and a WireGuard client in one. Arguably strictly better than NetGuard now.
tools.notes: Uses the VPN slot, so it conflicts with PCAPdroid and other VPN-mode apps.

tools.name: Tailscale
tools.desc: Mesh VPN over WireGuard with SSO. Gets the phone onto your homelab with no port forwarding.

tools.name: Tor Browser
tools.desc: The browser, not the proxy. Use with or without Orbot.
tools.notes: Not in the main F-Droid repo. The Guardian Project repo carries it too.

tools.name: Twingate
tools.desc: Zero-trust network access. Alternative path to the same homelab.

tools.name: WireGuard
tools.desc: The VPN you will actually use for lab and client access. Fast, simple config, no daemon to babysit.
tools.notes: Not in the main F-Droid repo. WireGuard run their own F-Droid-compatible repo at f-droid.wireguard.com if you would rather avoid Play.

tools.name: Chameleon Ultra GUI
tools.desc: Controls a Chameleon Ultra over BLE or USB. Slot management, card emulation, reads.

tools.name: Flipper Mobile App
tools.desc: Official companion for the Flipper Zero.

tools.name: MIFARE Classic Tool
tools.desc: Key dictionary attacks and sector dumping on MIFARE Classic. The core on-phone RFID tool.
tools.notes: Needs an NXP NFC controller. Many phones cannot read Classic at all.

tools.name: NFC Tools
tools.desc: Read, write and emulate NDEF tags. The PRO version adds tasks and scripting.

tools.name: nRF Connect for Mobile
tools.desc: The real BLE tool: scan, connect, enumerate services, read and write characteristics, log advertising. Not a generic 'BLE scanner'.
tools.notes: Pairs directly with any Nordic nRF development board.

tools.name: NXP TagInfo
tools.desc: Deep tag identification — chip type, memory layout, capability container.

tools.name: Serial USB Terminal
tools.desc: USB OTG serial console. This is how you talk to an ESP32, a Proxmark3, a Chameleon Ultra, or anything else with a UART.

tools.name: USB Device Info
tools.desc: Identify what is plugged into OTG and confirm the phone actually supports USB host mode.
tools.notes: Run this first — plenty of phones do not do USB host at all.

tools.name: Bluetooth HCI snoop log
tools.desc: Not an app. Enable the toggle in Developer Options, reproduce the pairing, then pull btsnoop_hci.log and open it in Wireshark.
tools.notes: adb bugreport, or adb pull /data/misc/bluetooth/logs/btsnoop_hci.log with Shizuku or root.

tools.name: Proxmark3 client
tools.desc: Compiles in Termux. The serial device permission is the hard part, not the build.
tools.notes: OTG serial access from Termux normally needs root or a udev-equivalent workaround.

tools.name: AndroGoat
tools.desc: Kotlin vulnerable app with a broad, well-labelled issue set.

tools.name: DIVA
tools.desc: Damn Insecure and Vulnerable App. The standard first target for Android app assessment practice.

tools.name: DVWA
tools.desc: The classic. Needs PHP and MariaDB in Termux, which is more setup than Juice Shop but works.

tools.name: InsecureBankv2
tools.desc: Vulnerable banking app with a companion backend, so you get network issues as well as app ones.

tools.name: InsecureShop
tools.desc: Modern intentionally vulnerable Android app, covering current issue classes rather than 2015 ones.

tools.name: OWASP Juice Shop
tools.desc: The web target. Node, so it runs directly in Termux with no Docker and no root.
tools.notes: In the TUR user repo, so run 'pkg install tur-repo' first. Docker does not work reliably on non-rooted Android, so do not build the lab story around it.

tools.name: PIVAA
tools.desc: Purposely Insecure and Vulnerable Android Application.

tools.name: OWASP MASTG Crackmes
tools.desc: UnCrackable levels 1 to 4. Root detection, anti-tamper, native code, obfuscation.
tools.notes: Levels 3 and 4 realistically need Frida, so Tier 2.

tools.name: VAmPI
tools.desc: Deliberately vulnerable API, Python. Good pairing with Reqable on the same device.

tools.name: APK Analyzer
tools.desc: Quick on-device look at permissions, activities, certificates and manifest.

tools.name: apksigner / zipalign
tools.desc: Re-sign and align a patched APK so the device will install it.
tools.notes: Under developer verification your own signing key will need to be registered to install on a certified device without the advanced flow.

tools.name: apktool
tools.desc: Smali disassembly and rebuild. For patching an app rather than just reading it.

tools.name: Ecliptic
tools.desc: Technology stack detection. First-party androidWTF tooling.

tools.name: jadx
tools.desc: Decompiles an APK to readable Java. Runs fine in Termux with a JDK, and this is where most mobile assessment actually starts.

tools.name: MobSF
tools.desc: Static and dynamic analysis framework. Technically runs in Termux; realistically run it on your homelab and reach it from the phone.
tools.notes: Heavy. A phone is the wrong place for this.

tools.name: On-device adb shell
tools.desc: Not an app. With Shizuku paired you get pm, dumpsys, content and settings from a local shell — most of what you would otherwise plug into a laptop for.

tools.name: Frida server
tools.desc: Runtime instrumentation — hook methods, dump arguments, bypass checks live.
tools.notes: The server binary needs root. The client can run in Termux or on your laptop.

tools.name: objection
tools.desc: Frida wrapper that does the common jobs without writing hooks: SSL pinning bypass, storage dump, class enumeration.

tools.name: CellMapper
tools.desc: Crowd-sourced cell site mapping and coverage data.

tools.name: Fing
tools.desc: Fast network discovery with good device fingerprinting. Heavy upsell, but the free tier does the job.

tools.name: HTTP Toolkit
tools.desc: Alternative intercepting proxy with strong ADB integration and one-click certificate setup.

tools.name: netcat / socat
tools.desc: The two tools you actually reach for. Listeners, relays, port forwards.
tools.notes: Ports below 1024 need root.

tools.name: Network Cell Info Lite
tools.desc: Cell tower mapping, band and signal detail, neighbouring cells.

tools.name: Network Survey
tools.desc: Cellular, WiFi, GNSS and Bluetooth survey with logging to file. Underrated for site surveys and RF mapping.

tools.name: nmap
tools.desc: The scanner. Connect scan works unprivileged; SYN scan, OS detection and anything raw-socket needs root.
tools.notes: nmap -sT works at Tier 0. nmap -sS needs Tier 2.

tools.name: PCAPdroid
tools.desc: Packet capture with no root, by running a local VPN service. Exports real PCAP for Wireshark. With root it captures the full interface instead of just app traffic.
tools.notes: Tier 0 gives you app traffic only. Tier 2 gives you the whole interface.

tools.name: Port Authority
tools.desc: Open source LAN scanner and port scanner.

tools.name: PortDroid
tools.desc: Port scanner, host discovery, DNS lookup, whois and traceroute in one app.

tools.name: Reqable
tools.desc: Modern on-device intercepting HTTP(S) proxy, the successor to HttpCanary. Inspect, rewrite and replay requests without a laptop.

tools.name: WiFiAnalyzer
tools.desc: Channel and signal analysis. Open source, no ads, no telemetry — prefer it over the closed alternatives.

tools.name: WiFiman
tools.desc: Ubiquiti's analyser. Clean, fast, with a good speed test and device discovery.

tools.name: bettercap
tools.desc: Network attack and MITM framework. Needs raw sockets for anything beyond passive use.

tools.name: masscan
tools.desc: Mass port scanner. Raw sockets only, so it is root-or-nothing.
tools.notes: Build from source; there is no Termux package.

tools.name: Responder
tools.desc: LLMNR, NBT-NS and MDNS poisoner.
tools.notes: Binds privileged ports, so root is mandatory.

tools.name: SnoopSnitch
tools.desc: IMSI catcher and SS7 attack detection from the baseband's own diagnostic messages.
tools.notes: Needs root and a Qualcomm chipset. Will not work on Exynos or Tensor.

tools.name: tcpdump
tools.desc: Interface capture from the shell. Needs raw socket access.
tools.notes: At Tier 0 use PCAPdroid instead.

tools.name: APRSdroid
tools.desc: Amateur packet radio over APRS-IS or a real TNC.
tools.notes: Not in the main F-Droid repo — take it from GitHub Releases.

tools.name: dump1090
tools.desc: ADS-B aircraft tracking off an RTL-SDR, from the Termux shell.

tools.name: GPSTest
tools.desc: GNSS constellation view, accuracy, and which satellite systems the phone actually uses.

tools.name: Look4Sat
tools.desc: Open source satellite pass prediction and tracking.

tools.name: Meshtastic
tools.desc: LoRa mesh networking. Talks to Heltec, T-Beam and RAK boards over BLE.

tools.name: NMEA Tools
tools.desc: Read an external GPS dongle over OTG and feed it to the system location provider.

tools.name: RepeaterBook
tools.desc: Amateur repeater directory with offline data.

tools.name: RF Analyzer
tools.desc: Open source spectrum analyser supporting RTL-SDR and HackRF.

tools.name: rtl_433
tools.desc: Decodes the 433MHz sensor soup — weather stations, TPMS, doorbells, remotes.

tools.name: RTL2832U driver
tools.desc: Martin Marinov's driver. A prerequisite for every RTL-SDR app on Android — install it before anything else in this category.

tools.name: SDR Touch
tools.desc: RTL-SDR receiver with a waterfall and demodulation. Free tier is time-limited.

tools.name: SDR++
tools.desc: Modern multi-SDR receiver, actively developed, supports most hardware.

tools.name: amass
tools.desc: Subdomain enumeration and attack surface mapping.

tools.name: Google Earth
tools.desc: Aerial and street-level site recon before a physical engagement.

tools.name: Organic Maps
tools.desc: Offline maps with no account and no tracking. For physical engagements where you need site layout with no signal.

tools.name: OsmAnd
tools.desc: Offline maps with heavier features — routing profiles, custom overlays, GPX recording.

tools.name: Sherlock
tools.desc: Username enumeration across hundreds of sites.

tools.name: Shodan
tools.desc: Host and service intelligence lookup.

tools.name: subfinder
tools.desc: Fast passive subdomain discovery.

tools.name: theHarvester
tools.desc: Email, subdomain and host gathering from public sources.

tools.name: MITRE ATT&CK for Mobile
tools.desc: Technique taxonomy, and the vocabulary clients expect findings mapped to.

tools.name: GTFOBins / LOLBAS
tools.desc: Living-off-the-land binaries for Unix and Windows.

tools.name: HackTricks
tools.desc: The single most useful practical reference. Mirror it offline — site work rarely has signal.

tools.name: KOReader
tools.desc: Document reader for the offline reference pack. Handles PDF, EPUB and HTML.

tools.name: Librera Reader
tools.desc: The alternative reader, better on large PDFs.

tools.name: NIST SP 800-115
tools.desc: Technical guide to information security testing. The methodology citation for a report.

tools.name: OWASP MASTG / MASVS
tools.desc: The mobile testing standard. Directly relevant to everything in the Mobile App Assessment category.

tools.name: OWASP WSTG / ASVS
tools.desc: The web testing standard, and the verification requirements to test against.

tools.name: PayloadsAllTheThings
tools.desc: Payload and technique reference by injection class.

tools.name: Exploit-DB / searchsploit
tools.desc: Offline exploit database with local search.

tools.name: SecLists
tools.desc: Wordlists. Mirror them locally — you will not want to download these on a client site.

tools.name: Amaze File Manager
tools.desc: Open source file manager, root-aware. The alternative to Material Files.

tools.name: KDE Connect
tools.desc: Shared clipboard, file push and remote input between the phone and your laptop.

tools.name: LocalSend
tools.desc: AirDrop-equivalent over the local network, cross platform, open source.

tools.name: Material Files
tools.desc: Open source file manager with SMB, SFTP and FTP built in. Actively maintained.

tools.name: Microsoft Remote Desktop
tools.desc: RDP into Windows targets and jump boxes.

tools.name: OpenSSH
tools.desc: sshd on the phone as well as ssh from it. The phone becomes something you can reach.
tools.notes: Must listen above port 1024 without root. 8022 is the Termux convention.

tools.name: RealVNC Viewer
tools.desc: Required for NetHunter KeX, and generally the most reliable VNC client on Android.

tools.name: rsync
tools.desc: Move artifacts around properly, resumable, over SSH.

tools.name: RustDesk
tools.desc: Open source remote desktop with a self-hostable relay. Fits a homelab better than any commercial option.

tools.name: Syncthing-Fork
tools.desc: Continuous peer-to-peer sync with no cloud. This is how engagement artifacts get off the phone and onto your homelab without touching a third party.
tools.notes: The original com.nutomic.syncthingandroid was discontinued and pulled from F-Droid. This fork is the maintained one.

tools.name: exiftool
tools.desc: Read, strip and verify metadata before anything goes into a report.

tools.name: Joplin
tools.desc: Open source notes with self-hostable sync. The alternative if you want the whole stack open.

tools.name: Markor
tools.desc: Lightweight markdown editor over local files. No database, no sync, no lock-in.

tools.name: Nextcloud
tools.desc: Self-hosted artifact storage, if you would rather have a server than peer sync.

tools.name: Obsidian
tools.desc: Markdown notes over a plain folder. Combined with Syncthing this is a complete engagement notes pipeline with no vendor in it.

tools.name: Open Camera
tools.desc: Manual camera with GPS stamping and EXIF control. For physical engagement evidence that has to hold up later.

tools.name: ADV Screen Recorder
tools.desc: Screen capture of exploitation steps, for the report and for proving it worked.

tools.name: Timestamp Camera
tools.desc: Burns date, time and coordinates into the image itself rather than only the metadata.

tools.name: Caddy
tools.desc: A real web server with automatic HTTPS, from the phone.

tools.name: Cowrie
tools.desc: SSH and Telnet honeypot that records the whole session. Python, so it runs in Termux.
tools.notes: Remap ports above 1024 at Tier 0, or bind the real ports at Tier 2.

tools.name: impacket
tools.desc: The Windows protocol toolkit. Most of it works; anything binding 445 needs root.

tools.name: Metasploit Framework
tools.desc: Installs and runs in Termux. Heavy, and listeners are limited to unprivileged ports without root.

tools.name: nginx
tools.desc: The other real web server, when you want the config you already know.

tools.name: ntfy
tools.desc: Self-hosted push notifications. This is what a honeypot or a canary token fires into.

tools.name: OpenCanary
tools.desc: Multi-protocol honeypot daemon. Pairs naturally with a canary token deployment.

tools.name: python -m http.server
tools.desc: Payload hosting and exfil endpoint in one command. Works unprivileged as long as the port is above 1024.

tools.name: nmap
tools.desc: Termux apt package. Proves the pkg path and gives you something obviously testable.
tools.notes: Verify with: nmap -sT -p 80,443 scanme.nmap.org

tools.name: httpie
tools.desc: Python package. Proves pip works and that the python toolchain step fires first.
tools.notes: Verify with: http --version

tools.name: ffuf
tools.desc: Go module. Proves the go toolchain installs and builds. Slowest step by far.
tools.notes: Compiles on device — allow several minutes. Verify with: ~/go/bin/ffuf -V

tools.name: PayloadsAllTheThings
tools.desc: Shallow clone. Proves the git path and the WTF_SRC directory. Small enough to be quick.
tools.notes: Lands in ~/wtf/src. Verify with: ls ~/wtf/src/PayloadsAllTheThings

tools.name: Hacker Tracker
tools.desc: DEF CON conference companion. Not a tool, but it is always on the phone anyway.

tools.name: Pentest Reference
tools.desc: Offline command and methodology reference. First-party androidWTF tooling.

tools.name: SpoofCard
tools.desc: Caller ID spoofing. The US Truth in Caller ID Act makes spoofing with intent to defraud or harm illegal, and the TRACED Act raised the penalties.
tools.notes: Requires written client authorisation naming caller ID spoofing as an in-scope technique. Most consumer spoofing services have also shut down or restricted signups.

tools.name: Trust Me Bro
tools.desc: Pretext soundboard. First-party androidWTF tooling.

tools.name: feroxbuster
tools.desc: Recursive content discovery in Rust.

tools.name: ffuf
tools.desc: Content and parameter fuzzing. Runs at full speed in Termux.

tools.name: Firefox Nightly
tools.desc: The only mainstream mobile browser that runs real desktop extensions. Wappalyzer, Cookie Editor, FoxyProxy and friends all work.
tools.notes: Custom add-on collections need a one-time setup in the debug menu.

tools.name: Hermit
tools.desc: Wraps any web app as a standalone lite app. Good for PortSwigger Academy, your own dashboards, or anything you want off the browser tab pile.

tools.name: httpx
tools.desc: Fast HTTP probing and fingerprinting across a host list.

tools.name: Kiwi Browser
tools.desc: Chromium with Chrome Web Store extension support. Development has been intermittent — treat Firefox Nightly as the primary.

tools.name: mitmproxy
tools.desc: Scriptable intercepting proxy from the shell, for when Reqable's UI is not enough.

tools.name: nikto
tools.desc: Old, noisy, still finds things.

tools.name: nuclei
tools.desc: Template-driven vulnerability scanning. Works well on a phone.

tools.name: sqlmap
tools.desc: SQL injection automation. Slow on a phone but entirely functional.

tools.name: URLCheck
tools.desc: Inspect, unshorten and strip tracking from a URL before it opens. Set it as the default handler.

tools.name: Burp / system CA install
tools.desc: Not an app. On Android 7+ user-added CAs are not trusted by apps, so an intercepting proxy sees nothing until the certificate lands in the system store.
tools.notes: Magisk modules like AlwaysTrustUserCerts handle this. At Tier 0 you are limited to apps that opt into user CAs.

tools.name: Muon
tools.desc: Terminal WiFi manager, first-party. Brings adapters up and down, toggles monitor mode, matches chipsets against a driver database, and puts 100+ wireless and pentest commands behind a menu with variable substitution — so you stop typing airodump-ng syntax from memory.
tools.notes: Single Python 3 file, no pip dependencies. Detects two modes at launch: full with root, limited without. In limited mode the root-only actions are greyed out rather than hidden, and you still get scanning, the command reference, the adapter/driver database and the troubleshooting guide. Termux limited mode also wants 'pkg install termux-api' and the Termux:API app.

tools.name: WiFi Warden
tools.desc: WPS analysis and network detail. Legally sensitive — connecting to a network you do not own is a CFAA problem regardless of how easy the app makes it.
tools.notes: Authorised engagements only, with the technique named in scope.

tools.name: WiGLE WiFi Wardriving
tools.desc: Logs every network you drive past with GPS, and exports CSV. Works on a completely stock phone.

tools.name: aircrack-ng suite
tools.desc: The classic wireless attack suite. Everything in it needs monitor mode.
tools.notes: Internal Android chipsets do not do monitor mode. You need a NetHunter kernel, and in practice an external adapter over OTG.

tools.name: hcxdumptool
tools.desc: PMKID and handshake capture, the modern path to WPA2 material.
tools.notes: Capture on the phone, crack on your homelab. There is no usable GPU path on Android.

tools.name: Kismet
tools.desc: Wireless detector, sniffer and IDS. Wants monitor mode on a real interface.

tools.name: Wifite2
tools.desc: Automation wrapper over the aircrack suite. Same monitor mode requirement.
